Men’s Pedicure Selection: Base Options, Finish, and Booking Notes

A practical guide to pedicure for men, including service fit, preparation, maintenance, and verified Element 16 visit details.

By Element Nail Bar Editorial TeamSeptember 5, 2026Updated September 22, 20266 min read

In this guide

pedicure selection for menCompare services →View menu & pricing →

What to know

Element Nail Bar’s current booking catalog does not list a separate pedicure for men. A guest can choose from the same eight base pedicures and then select any relevant pedicure add-ons. For a first visit, compare the exact service name, listed price, total duration, included regular-polish finish, and any extra option you want rather than looking for a gendered package.

You also do not have to choose color. The catalog includes a separately bookable Shinny Buff option, and the salon can explain the available no-color finish before the appointment. The most useful first step is to decide how much time you want to reserve and tell the salon what is already on the toenails.

Pick a base reservation first

There are eight current base pedicures in Element 16 online booking. Classic Pedicure is $35 for 25 minutes. Deluxe Pedicure is $49 for 40 minutes. Organic Spa Pedicure is $65 for 50 minutes. Pearl Spa Pedicure is $75 for 60 minutes. Róse Berry Pedicure is $85 for 65 minutes. Jelly Spa Pedicure is $90 for 70 minutes. CBD Experience Pedicure is $105 for 75 minutes. Gold Enchantment Pedicure is $120 for 85 minutes.

Regular polish is included with each of those base services. Optional add-ons are booked separately. The catalog does not publish the full product recipe, massage length, tool sequence, or included skin-care steps for any base pedicure, so choose by the confirmed listing and ask the salon when an unlisted detail matters to you.

A straightforward first-time approach is to start with the duration and budget that suit the visit. The longer listing is not automatically the better choice. It simply reserves a different named service for a different price and total time.

Decide whether you want a finish add-on

Regular polish is the included finish. Gel Polish is available as a $15, 15-minute pedicure add-on. French is also listed at $15 for 15 minutes, and Shinny Buff is $10 for 15 minutes. Tell the salon which finish you want when you book so the appointment reflects both the base service and the added time.

If product is already on the toenails, describe it as accurately as you can. Say whether it appears to be regular polish, gel, or an enhancement. Mention a repair request rather than assuming it belongs inside a base pedicure. The booking catalog separately lists Toes Repair, Toes Fill, and Toes Fullset, so the correct category may depend on what is currently present.

Do not peel or force off existing product before the appointment. If you are unsure what it is, a photo or a brief call can help the salon tell you what information to put in the reservation. The technician can then confirm the cosmetic plan after seeing the toenails.

Add only what you actually want

The pedicure menu includes optional additions beyond the finish. Callus Removal is listed at $10 for 15 minutes. Sugar Scrubs is $10 for 15 minutes. Paraffin Hot Wax is $15 for 15 minutes. Extra Massage is available in separate five- and ten-minute listings, and Hot Stone Massage has its own five-minute listing.

Those are independent catalog entries. Their existence does not mean they are included in a base pedicure, and this guide does not assign them to one. If an add-on is the main reason you are visiting, select it explicitly or ask the salon how to attach it to the chosen base reservation.

Booking only the options you want also makes the estimate easier to understand. A base price is not a promise that every finished appointment will cost that amount. Added time, finish choices, removal, repairs, or enhancement work can change the final scope.

What to put in a first booking note

A useful note is short, factual, and easy for the front desk to interpret. Include details such as:

  • whether this is your first salon pedicure;
  • what product, if any, is already on the toenails;
  • the exact base pedicure name you selected;
  • regular polish, Gel Polish, French, Shinny Buff, or no color;
  • a known repair or enhancement request;
  • an add-on you intentionally selected;
  • a request for nearby seats when booking with another guest; and
  • any ingredient sensitivity or comfort preference the salon should know before service.

For example: “First pedicure, Classic Pedicure, no existing product, Shinny Buff instead of color.” Another clear note is: “Deluxe Pedicure, existing gel, new Gel Polish, please confirm the correct removal option.” Neither note requires special salon vocabulary.

Questions that are normal on a first visit

You can ask about clothing, footwear, finish choices, or what to bring. Comfortable clothes are enough. If you select regular polish, ask the salon what footwear will best protect the fresh finish after the appointment. If you select Gel Polish, remember that a later change may involve a different removal plan.

You can also ask for an explanation before agreeing to an added service. A name on the menu may not answer every practical question. Ask what has been selected, how much time it adds, and what it costs. Clear confirmation at the beginning avoids a mismatch between the reservation and the result you expected.

Comfort preferences are appropriate to mention. Tell the technician if pressure, water temperature, or positioning is uncomfortable. A cosmetic appointment is not medical care. Pain, infection, fungus, broken skin, or another health concern calls for appropriate medical advice instead of routine cosmetic service.

Ask directly about cleanliness procedures

This article does not state that a particular liner, file, buffer, implement, disinfectant, or sanitation sequence is used. Those operating details are not in the active booking catalog. If they affect your decision, ask Element Nail Bar directly for its current cleaning, sanitation, and single-use-item procedures before the visit.

That question is reasonable for any guest and does not require a special first-time script. Listen for a clear explanation of current practice. A general marketing phrase is not evidence of a specific operating procedure.

Plan the Phoenix visit

Element Nail Bar is at 6022 N 16th St, Phoenix, AZ 85016. Current site hours are Monday through Saturday from 9:30 AM to 7:00 PM and Sunday from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Call 602-607-5686 when the base service, existing product, or add-on category is unclear.

Phoenix routines may affect the finish or timing you prefer. Sandals, closed work shoes, pool plans, travel, and an upcoming event are practical reasons to discuss polish and appointment timing. They do not change which services the catalog offers, and they do not support promises about wear or health outcomes.

Review the current pedicure options and the live menu before reserving. When the selection is clear, [book the Element 16 appointment](/book-now/) with the base service and relevant additions named in the note. A precise reservation—not a “men’s” label—is what helps the salon prepare for the visit.
